rows: Detail of an Industrial Building in Massachusetts
Jack Delano photographed the brick and windows of a factory building in Massachusetts in 1939 for the Farm Security Administration. The repeating windows make a pattern against the sky.
How many windows can you count?
Street Scene, Mystic, Connecticut
Jack Delano photographed a street in Mystic, Connecticut, in 1939. The seaport town was known for shipbuilding.
What would you see on a main street in a port town?
Children with an Adult in the Tenement District, Brockton, Massachusetts
Jack Delano photographed children and an adult in a crowded neighborhood in Brockton, Massachusetts, in 1939. Brockton was a shoe-making city, and many workers lived in tenements.
What would it be like to live in a crowded neighborhood?
Douglas Shoe Factory, Brockton, Massachusetts
Jack Delano photographed the Douglas shoe factory in Brockton in 1939. Brockton produced more shoes than any other city in the United States.
How many shoes would a factory make in a day?
Copper Mining and Sulfuric Acid Plant, Copperhill, Tennessee
Marion Post Wolcott photographed a copper mine and sulfuric acid plant at Copperhill, Tennessee, in 1939. The fumes from the smelters had killed the plants on the hills around.
How can factories change the land around them?
A Train Bringing Copper Ore from the Mine, Ducktown, Tennessee
Marion Post Wolcott photographed a train carrying copper ore out of the mines at Ducktown, Tennessee, in 1939. Mining here began in the 1840s.
What is copper used for?
Black Tenant's Home beside the Mississippi River Levee
Marion Post Wolcott photographed the home of a Black tenant farmer by the Mississippi River levee in 1939. Levees are high banks that protect fields from floods.
How would you feel living next to a levee?
Bayou Bourbeau Plantation, a Cooperative
Marion Post Wolcott photographed Bayou Bourbeau, a farm cooperative in Louisiana, in 1939. The Farm Security Administration helped farmers pool resources.
What does it mean to work in a cooperative?
Fishing in a Creek near Cotton Plantations
Marion Post Wolcott photographed Black people fishing in a creek outside Belzoni, Mississippi, in 1939. Fishing brought food and a break from field work.
What would you catch in a creek?
Going to Town on Saturday Afternoon, Greene County, Georgia
Jack Delano photographed a family going to town in a wagon in Greene County, Georgia, in 1939. Saturday was the day rural families went to shop and meet friends.
What would you do in town on Saturday?
Chopping Cotton on Rented Land
Jack Delano photographed workers chopping cotton on rented land near White Plains in Greene County, Georgia, in 1939. Chopping means thinning the rows of cotton by hoe.
Why is chopping cotton hard work?
Grain Elevators, Caldwell, Idaho
Russell Lee photographed grain elevators in Caldwell, Idaho, in 1939. These tall storage buildings hold the harvest of local farms.
Why would grain need to be stored high?
Flour Mill, Caldwell, Idaho
Russell Lee photographed a flour mill in Caldwell, Idaho, in 1939. Mills turn wheat into flour.
How is wheat turned into flour?
Cherry Orchards and Farming Land, Emmett, Idaho
Russell Lee photographed orchards in Emmett, Idaho, in 1939. Irrigation from the river turned the dry valley into farmland.
Why do orchards need irrigation?
Main Street of Cascade, Idaho
Russell Lee photographed the main street of Cascade, Idaho, in 1939. The small mountain town sits by a reservoir in the Salmon River country.
What would shops on a mountain street sell?
Wheat Farm, Walla Walla, Washington
Russell Lee photographed a wheat farm near Walla Walla, Washington, in 1939. Rolling hills are planted with golden wheat.
What does a wheat field look like in the wind?
Canning Plant for Peas, Milton-Freewater
Russell Lee photographed a pea cannery in Milton-Freewater, Oregon, in 1939. Peas were a main crop in the valley.
How do you get peas into a can?
Parachute Instructor, Meacham Field, Fort Worth
Arthur Rothstein photographed an instructor explaining a parachute to students at Meacham Field in Fort Worth, Texas, in 1939. A civilian pilot training program prepared pilots before the war.
Would you want to learn to fly?
Student Pilots, Meacham Field, Fort Worth
Arthur Rothstein photographed student pilots at Meacham Field, Fort Worth, Texas, in 1939. The government paid for civilian flying lessons.
What would you learn first as a pilot?
Civilian Pilot Training School, Returning from Practice Flight
Student pilots walk back from a practice flight at Meacham Field, Fort Worth, in 1939. Planes in the background sit on the field.
What would you feel after your first flight?
Instructor and Students Studying a Map
Arthur Rothstein photographed an instructor and students studying a map at Meacham Field in 1939. Pilots had to learn to navigate.
How would you find your way in the sky?
Families of Migratory Workers in Front of Row Shelters

Arthur Rothstein photographed families of migratory workers in front of their row shelters at a Farm Security Administration camp in Robstown, Texas, in 1939. The camps gave workers decent places to live.
Why would a camp be better than living in a car?
Boys Playing Marbles, Robstown, Texas
Arthur Rothstein photographed boys playing marbles at a labor camp in Robstown, Texas, in 1939. Kids still found games in hard times.
How do you play marbles?
Gardens in Front of the Row Shelters
Residents of the Robstown labor camp planted gardens in front of the row shelters in 1939. The government camp encouraged gardening.
What would you plant outside your home?
Cultivating a Field, Seabrook Farm
John Collier photographed a worker cultivating a field at Seabrook Farm in Bridgeton, New Jersey, in 1939. Seabrook was one of the biggest vegetable farms in America.
How do you cultivate a field?
Bean Field and Canning Factory, Seabrook Farm
John Collier photographed a bean field next to a canning factory at Seabrook Farm in 1939. The farm and factory were joined for freezing and canning vegetables.
Why build a factory right next to the field?
Day Laborers Picking String Beans
John Collier photographed day laborers, some from nearby towns and others migrants, picking string beans at Seabrook Farm in 1939. They worked from early morning.
How many beans would you pick in a day?
Low-Flying Plane Spreading Dust or Insecticide
John Collier photographed a low-flying plane spreading dust or insecticide over crops at Seabrook Farm in 1939. Crop dusting was new, and planes covered fields quickly.
Why would a farmer use a plane?
Shot Putter, University of Nebraska
John Vachon photographed a shot putter at the University of Nebraska around 1939. Track and field was a big sport at Midwest colleges.
What does a shot put weigh?
Girl with Doll by a Fence
A girl stands by a fence holding her doll in a rural scene from the late 1930s. The photograph was made for the Farm Security Administration.
What would you do with a doll in a field?
Sunflower Plants
A field of sunflowers stands tall in a photograph from the Farm Security Administration around 1939. Sunflowers turn to face the sun.
Why do sunflowers follow the sun?
Cows on a Hillside
Cows graze on a green hillside in a photograph for the Farm Security Administration in 1939. Dairy farms were a mainstay of rural America.
What does a cow eat all day?
Black Troops at the Memorial Day Parade, Washington, D.C.
Royden Dixon photographed Black soldiers marching in a Memorial Day parade in Washington, D.C., in 1939. Black Americans served in segregated units in the U.S. military.
Why did the military separate soldiers?
Christmas Trees and Wreaths in a Store Window
Christmas trees and wreaths fill a store window in a 1939 photograph. Holiday displays drew shoppers even in the late Depression.
How do shops decorate for the holidays?
Preparing for Take-Off at Glider Pilot Training
Alfred T. Palmer photographed Marines preparing for a glider take-off at the training program at Parris Island, South Carolina. Gliders have no engines and are towed into the sky by airplanes.
How does a glider stay up with no engine?
Marine Corps Gliders in Flight
Alfred T. Palmer photographed Marine Corps gliders in flight over Parris Island, South Carolina. The gliders float behind tow planes.
What does it look like to see a plane towing a glider?
Electric Phosphate Smelting Furnace
Alfred T. Palmer photographed a large electric phosphate smelting furnace used to make elemental phosphorus. The furnace glows as workers handle it.
What is phosphorus used for?
Girl Inspector at an Aircraft Plant
Alfred T. Palmer photographed a woman inspector examining aircraft parts at a plant in Long Beach, California. During the war many women worked in factories.
How would you check a part for flaws?
Garden of the Pan American Union Building

John Collier photographed the garden of the Pan American Union building in Washington, D.C. The building, with a tropical patio, was home to the organization that later became the Organization of American States.
Why would a garden have tropical plants?
Berry House, Selma, Alabama
Frances Benjamin Johnston photographed the Berry House in Selma, Alabama, for her survey of the Early Architecture of the South. Selma had many old buildings.
What would you notice about an old house?
St. James Hotel, Selma, Alabama
Frances Benjamin Johnston photographed the St. James Hotel in Selma, Alabama, in 1939. The three-story brick hotel stands beside the Alabama River.
Why would a hotel be built beside a river?
Riverdale Plantation, near Selma
Frances Benjamin Johnston photographed Riverdale Plantation near Selma, Alabama, in the late 1930s. She documented old southern houses for the Carnegie Survey of the Architecture of the South.
Why would someone photograph old houses?
Fashion Model Underwater with a Diver in a Dolphin Tank
Toni Frissell photographed a fashion model underwater with a diver in the dolphin tank at Marineland, Florida, in 1939. She tried odd places for fashion photographs.
Would you pose underwater?
Fashion Model Underwater, Marineland
Toni Frissell photographed a fashion model floating underwater in the dolphin tank at Marineland, Florida. Frissell took fashion photographs in outdoor and unusual spots.
How would you pose in water?
A Rainy Day in Providence, Rhode Island
Britt Fuller photographed Providence, Rhode Island, in a downpour in December 1940. Rain on streets and roofs makes a moody scene.
What does a rainy city sound like?
Agnes Sligh Turnbull
This is a seated portrait of Agnes Sligh Turnbull, an American author of novels about small-town life, around 1940. She wrote The Rolling Years.
What kind of stories would you tell about your town?
Orson Welles with Virginia and Christopher
Orson Welles, who directed Citizen Kane, poses with his wife Virginia and their daughter Christopher around 1940. He had become famous with his radio broadcast of The War of the Worlds in 1938.
Why would a radio show scare listeners?
Twelfth Street YMCA, Lounge
This photograph shows the lounge inside the Twelfth Street YMCA in Washington, D.C., around 1940. The YMCA was an important gathering place for Black Washingtonians.
Why would a community center matter?
A Street Corner in Burlington, Vermont
Jack Delano photographed a street corner in Burlington, Vermont, in 1941 for the Farm Security Administration. A few cars and shops line the busy corner.
What shops would you find on a corner?
A Slate Quarry near Castleton, Vermont
Jack Delano photographed a slate quarry near Castleton, Vermont, in 1941. Slate is cut into roofing tiles and blackboards.
What would you use slate for?
French-Canadian Farmers in Vermont
Jack Delano photographed French-Canadian farmers in Vermont in 1941. Many families had moved from Quebec to work the dairy farms of the region.
Why do families move to another country?
Flock in Owens Valley, California
Ansel Adams photographed a flock of sheep in the Owens Valley, California, in 1941. The sheep trail over the dry valley below the Sierra Nevada.
What do shepherds do all day?
Main Street, Enosburg Falls, Vermont
Jack Delano photographed the main street of Enosburg Falls, Vermont, in 1941. The town was known for a patent medicine company.
What do you see along the street?
Walpi, Arizona
Ansel Adams photographed Walpi, a Hopi village on a high mesa in Arizona, in 1941. The pueblo has been lived in for hundreds of years.
How would it be to live on top of a mesa?
The Battle of Waterloo Road
This is the cover of The Battle of Waterloo Road, a 1941 book about the London Blitz by the photographer Robert Capa. Capa photographed war around the world.
Why would a war photographer take such risks?
Road on the Outskirts of Brattleboro, Vermont
Jack Delano photographed a road on the edge of Brattleboro, Vermont, in 1941. Hills and a bend invite the eye.
Where do you think the road leads?
Winter Corner, Brockton, Massachusetts
Britt Fuller photographed a snowy street corner in Brockton, Massachusetts, in January 1941. Brockton winters are cold.
What do you wear on a winter day?
Sir Winston Churchill
This portrait shows Winston Churchill, the British prime minister during World War II, around 1941. His speeches inspired Britain.
Why did people need inspiring speeches in the war?
5000 Danish Seamen Sailing for the United Nations
Louise Dahl-Wolfe photographed the Danish seamen who sailed with the Allies in 1942. Denmark had been occupied, but its sailors joined the war effort.
Why would sailors leave an occupied country?
William Lyon Mackenzie King
Prime Minister William Lyon Mackenzie King of Canada, photographed in 1942. He led Canada through World War II.
What does a prime minister do?
Women Working in a Needlework Factory, Santurce
Jack Delano photographed women working in a needlework factory in Santurce, Puerto Rico, in January 1942. Needlework was an important industry for women on the island.
What would you embroider?
Portrait of a Young Man, Southwest Washington, D.C.
Gordon Parks photographed a young Black man in Washington, D.C., in 1942. Parks was the first Black photographer on the Farm Security Administration staff.
What would you ask the young man?
A. Philip Randolph
Gordon Parks photographed A. Philip Randolph, the labor leader, in Washington, D.C., in 1942. Randolph led the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters and later organized the March on Washington.
What does a labor leader do?
Lincoln, Nebraska
John Vachon photographed a street in Lincoln, Nebraska, in 1942. The year can be told from the license plates of the cars.
How can a license plate tell the year?
Grocery Store, Mount Orab, Ohio
John Vachon photographed a small grocery store along Route 74 in Mount Orab, Ohio, in 1942. Signs on the front advertise products of the day.
What would you buy at a grocery in 1942?
Eagle Fruit Store and Capital Hotel, Lincoln
John Vachon photographed the Eagle Fruit Store and the Capital Hotel in Lincoln, Nebraska, in 1942. The block has shop signs and cars lined up.
What do the signs tell you?
Cemetery at the Edge of Romney, West Virginia
John Vachon photographed a hillside cemetery at the edge of Romney, West Virginia, in 1942. Gravestones stand on a hill above the town.
Why are cemeteries on hills?
Church near Junction City, Kansas
John Vachon photographed a country church near Junction City, Kansas, in 1942. The plain white church stands alone in a wide landscape.
Why would a church stand alone in a field?
Seed and Feed Store, Lincoln, Nebraska
John Vachon photographed a seed and feed store in Lincoln, Nebraska, in 1942. Farmers bought seed, grain and supplies there.
What would a farmer buy at a feed store?
Engineer Climbing into the Cab of His Engine, Cicero, Illinois
Jack Delano photographed a locomotive engineer climbing into his engine in Cicero, Illinois, in 1943. Railroads were crucial for moving people and supplies during the war.
What would you check before starting a locomotive?
Lord Woolton
Yousuf Karsh photographed Frederick Marquis, the 1st Earl of Woolton, who was Britain's Minister of Food in World War II. He ran the rationing system.
What is rationing?
Double-Header Pennsylvania Railroad Train, Chicago
Jack Delano photographed a double-header Pennsylvania Railroad train, two locomotives pulling together, in Chicago in 1943. Big trains were needed for wartime freight.
Why would a train have two engines?
Enlisted Personnel Exercise on the Flight Deck of USS Lexington
Edward Steichen photographed sailors exercising on the flight deck of the aircraft carrier USS Lexington in 1943. Steichen led a team of photographers for the U.S. Navy.
How would you exercise on a ship?
Chart Room of USS Lexington
Edward Steichen photographed the chart room of the USS Lexington in 1943. Navigators plotted the ship's path on charts.
How do you plan a path on the ocean?
Rear Admiral John S. McCain Sr.
Edward Steichen photographed Rear Admiral John S. McCain Sr. in 1943. McCain's son and grandson also became admirals and senators.
Why would a family have many sailors?
Lexington Pilots Celebrate Aerial Victories
Edward Steichen photographed pilots of the USS Lexington celebrating in 1943 after air battles. Their faces show relief and joy.
What would you do after a hard day's work?
Inspection Aboard a U.S. Submarine, New London
Edward Steichen photographed sailors lined up for inspection on a U.S. submarine at New London, Connecticut, in 1943. Submarine crews lived in tight quarters.
What would it be like to live on a submarine?
Princess Elizabeth
Yousuf Karsh photographed Princess Elizabeth in 1943, when she was a teenager. She became Queen Elizabeth II in 1952.
How does a photographer capture a future queen?
Viscount Alanbrooke
Yousuf Karsh photographed Alan Brooke, 1st Viscount Alanbrooke, the chief of Britain's Imperial General Staff, in the 1940s. Brooke guided British strategy in World War II.
What does the portrait tell you about his job?
F6F Going Down the Deck for Take-Off
A U.S. Navy photographer made this picture of an F6F Hellcat fighter speeding down the flight deck of USS Lexington in 1943. Taking off from a ship was tricky.
How does a plane take off on such a short runway?
ATSF 5000 Madam Queen
Jack Delano photographed the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe locomotive Number 5000, called Madam Queen, in 1943. The huge steam engine had a 2-10-4 wheel arrangement.
What does a steam locomotive sound like?
USS North Carolina Underway in the Gilbert Islands
The battleship USS North Carolina steams through the Pacific near the Gilbert Islands in November 1943. The ship's big guns are pointed out to sea.
Why are battleships so large?
Rex Stewart
Gordon Parks photographed Rex Stewart, a trumpeter with Duke Ellington's orchestra, in 1943. Stewart was known for his half-valve trumpet sound.
How would you make a trumpet sound different?
Pilots Leaning Across an F6F on the USS Lexington
Edward Steichen photographed pilots leaning across an F6F Hellcat on the USS Lexington in 1943. They are relaxed and ready.
How would you relax before a flight?
Bus Driver, Daytona Beach, Florida
Gordon Parks photographed a bus driver in Daytona Beach, Florida, in 1943 for the Office of War Information. His portrait shows his uniform and pride.
What do you think about the driver's job?
Richard Wright
Gordon Parks photographed Richard Wright in New York in 1943. Wright was the author of Native Son and Black Boy.
Have you read a book by Richard Wright?
Main Street, Gloucester, Massachusetts
Gordon Parks photographed the main street of Gloucester, Massachusetts, in 1943. The fishing town has narrow streets by the harbor.
What jobs do people have in a fishing town?
Portuguese Family, Gloucester
Gordon Parks photographed a Portuguese family in Gloucester, Massachusetts, in 1943. Many fishermen of Gloucester came from Portuguese families.
How do families keep traditions in a new country?
Women Workers Checking In, New Britain, Connecticut
Gordon Parks photographed women workers checking in at the Fafnir Bearing Company in New Britain, Connecticut, in 1943. During the war women filled factory jobs.
Why were so many women needed in factories?
Children Playing in a Fountain, Dupont Circle
Esther Bubley photographed children playing in a fountain at Dupont Circle in Washington, D.C., in 1943. The splashing was a relief on a hot summer day.
How do you cool off in summer?
Waiting for a Bus at the Greyhound Terminal, Pittsburgh
Esther Bubley photographed passengers waiting at a Greyhound bus terminal in Pittsburgh in 1943. She traveled by Greyhound bus in 1943 to document wartime travel for the Office of War Information.
What would you do while waiting for a bus?
A Starter Calling Buses, Pittsburgh
Esther Bubley photographed a starter calling out buses at the Greyhound terminal in Pittsburgh in 1943. The starter announced departures.
How do airports announce flights today?
A Greyhound Bus Driver Loading the Bus, Columbus
Esther Bubley photographed a Greyhound bus driver loading luggage in Columbus, Ohio, in 1943. Buses carried many wartime travelers.
How would you pack a bus?
Waiting for the Bus, Cincinnati
Esther Bubley photographed travelers waiting for a bus at the Greyhound terminal in Cincinnati in 1943. Soldiers, workers and families crowd the benches.
Who do you think is traveling?
Passengers Boarding a Greyhound Bus, Cincinnati
Esther Bubley photographed passengers boarding a Greyhound bus at the Cincinnati terminal in 1943. Wartime travel was crowded, because gas was rationed and trains were full.
Why was bus travel so crowded?
Bus Trip from Knoxville to Washington
Esther Bubley photographed passengers on a bus trip from Knoxville, Tennessee, to Washington, D.C., in 1943. Riders dozed, read and chatted over the long ride.
What would you do on a long bus ride?
LCVP from a Landing Ship, Normandy
A U.S. Navy photographer made this photograph of a landing craft carrying troops to the beaches of Normandy in 1944. LCVPs, or Higgins boats, carried soldiers from ships to shore on D-Day.
What would it be like to ride toward a beach under fire?
Henry L. Stimson
Yousuf Karsh photographed Henry L. Stimson, U.S. Secretary of War, in 1944. Stimson oversaw the American army in World War II.
What does a Secretary of War do?
Face in the Surf
Robert Capa photographed an American soldier in the water at Omaha Beach on D-Day, June 6, 1944. The soldier is crawling through the surf, with the beach under fire.
What was the soldier probably thinking?
Charles de Gaulle
Yousuf Karsh photographed Charles de Gaulle, leader of the Free French, in 1944. De Gaulle later became president of France.
What does a leader's face show?
George C. Marshall
Yousuf Karsh photographed General George C. Marshall, Army chief of staff in World War II. After the war Marshall created the Marshall Plan to rebuild Europe.
Why would a general want to rebuild countries?
